packageRules.description: Label majors so renovate-alert.yml can word a failure as a BREAKING change. Majors only open once approved on the Dependency Dashboard (`major` above) — unapproved breaking majors used to churn CI, spam alerts and hold PR slots.
Auto-merge npm (dev + runtime) on green — the real suite (unit + integration + e2e on a live stack) is the gate.

Keep lockstep monorepo siblings together (scripts/sync-monorepo-siblings.mjs). Security fixes are FORCED into per-package branches (vulnerabilityAlerts groupName:null — packageRules can't override it), so e.g. vitest got bumped without @vitest/coverage-v8 (exact peer) and both that PR and the grouped PR broke `npm ci`. The task moves same-repo, same-version siblings along and rewrites the lockfile with CI's npm. Allowed via RENOVATE_ALLOWED_COMMANDS in renovate.yml.

Group ALL non-major npm updates into ONE PR (every npm PR touches package-lock.json; siblings conflict the moment one merges). High priority: this PR + lockFileMaintenance carry most transitive security fixes, so they must never be starved by prConcurrentLimit (2026-07→10 they were — the loop deadlocked).
Lock file maintenance first: it refreshes every transitive (most npm audit fixes land here).
GitHub Actions auto-merge on green, majors included (CI exercises every workflow it touches).

Runner OS (`runs-on: ubuntu-24.04`, pinned so GitHub's ubuntu-latest flips don't change CI under us): an OS move needs Dependency Dashboard approval — PR CI exercises ci.yml on the new runner, but not deploy-production/trivy/renovate.

Docker default: images CI can't verify (cloudflared, studio, cadvisor, nginxlog-exporter, node in monitoring) wait for Dependency Dashboard approval instead of opening a PR — an unreviewed open PR holds a prConcurrentLimit slot forever. Approved → PR → manual merge. Overridden below for candidate-tested images.

The app's Dockerfile base images (node, docker/dockerfile): CI builds the image and runs e2e against it on every PR, so patch/minor/digest auto-merge on green (base-image OS CVEs — e.g. Alpine openssl — land via these). Ordered AFTER the docker default so it wins.

Node within the same major, everywhere it's pinned (Dockerfile, setup-node node-version, monitoring compose): Renovate groups these into one `node` branch, and without this rule the untested monitoring copy made the whole group (incl. base-image OS CVE fixes) wait for approval. CI exercises the Dockerfile + setup-node copies; the monitoring copy only runs a small PSI push script.

Infra images WITH a candidate test (Tier-1 config-boot / Tier-2 DB-coupled): auto-merge patch/minor/digest, gated by the REQUIRED 'Tier-1 candidate boot' check. Ordered AFTER the docker default so it wins. Majors stay approval-gated.

Stateful trio (postgres/gotrue/storage-api): gated by the Tier-3 MIGRATION-COMPAT candidate test (same required check). Auto-merge patch/minor/digest on green — this lands the tested version in the REPO only; the prod apply stays the manual rehearsed runbook (backup → swap → verify → rollback). Majors stay approval-gated (a postgres major needs pg_upgrade, which Tier-3 will correctly fail).
Renovate's own version (RENOVATE_VERSION in renovate.yml): keep the bot current — non-major auto-merges.
RENOVATE_VERSION is a plain version string fed to the action, not an image ref we run — no digest pin.
